name: Kenya
headline: Kenya: +4.6% growth in 2025, 4.1% inflation, debt 71% of GDP
sections: Kenya is a $136 billion economy (2025), the world's 64th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +4.6% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $7,016 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 7.1% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 4.1% in 2025, above typical targets, down from 7.6% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 5.4% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 15.2% (2025).
Gross government debt is 71% of GDP (2025), a elevated level that has risen from 68% in 2020. The general government balance is −6.5% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −2.8% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 38% of GDP (2025), a relatively closed economy. Net FDI inflows were 0.8% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 74% of GDP by 2031, broadly stable from today's level. Life expectancy is 63.8 years (2024). Population: 53.4 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
